title: The Crab Derby, 2002
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Eighteenth annual. Gully's derby now. He pays twenty. Wood takes it. The deal is back.

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY, apron, a twenty held out. WOOD. Four flyers on the wall.

balloons.text: Eighteen. Same crab. Twenty bucks. Take it this time.

image.prompt: a young man in a fisherman's apron holding out a twenty-dollar bill in front of a shingle shack with four crab flyers on the wall, brush-pen black and white
close-up of a hand slowly taking a twenty-dollar bill from another hand

panels.composition: The crab, drawn on the counter. Same crab. This year, for the first time, a second, smaller crab beside it. Gully sees it.
props: flyer with a large crab and a small one

image.prompt: a young man drawing a crab flyer on a shack counter where a second smaller crab has appeared beside the usual large one, a friend looking over his shoulder

panels.composition: Five flyers on the wall. The fifth has two crabs. Gully pinning it. The dog.

image.prompt: five crab flyers in a row on a shingle wall, the newest with two crabs, a young man in an apron pinning it, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; xerox; black and white

notes: Two crabs. The deal restored. The strip's economy is twenty dollars and one drawing a year.
